```{r setup}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(PKNCA)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Vicente B, Zazo H, Sanchez-Hernandez JG, Revilla N,
  Teixeira-da-Silva P. Population Pharmacokinetics of Subcutaneous
  Infliximab: A Real-World Study of Naive and Switch Patients.
  Pharmaceutics. 2026;18(9):1162.
* Article: [doi:10.3390/pharmaceutics18091162](https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18091162)
  (open access)

Vicente et al. developed a population PK model for subcutaneous
infliximab (SC-IFX, CT-P13 SC) from routine therapeutic drug monitoring
data in adults with inflammatory bowel disease treated at two Spanish
hospitals. The cohort mixed anti-TNF-naive patients who started SC
maintenance after IV induction with patients switched from IV
maintenance; the IV records of both groups were part of the dataset.
Because almost every sample was a pre-dose trough, the SC absorption
rate constant was fixed to the value of the pivotal Hanzel 2021 model
(see `Hanzel_2021_infliximab` in this package) after a sensitivity
analysis (Table S1), and IIV on V and on F was held at zero.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Vicente_2026_infliximab")
mod
```

# Population

Vicente 2026 Table 1: 45 adults (31.1% female) contributing 250 serum
infliximab concentrations (median 6 per patient). Median age 56 years
(IQR 38-61), median total body weight 74 kg (IQR 65-82), BMI 26.1
kg/m^2. Ulcerative colitis 64.4%, Crohn's disease 35.6%. Sixteen
patients (35.5%) were anti-TNF-naive and 29 (64.5%) were switched from
IV maintenance, most of them on intensified IV regimens (5-10 mg/kg
every 4-8 weeks). SC maintenance was 120 mg every 2 weeks, with
TDM-guided intervals (weekly, every 10 days or every 3 weeks) in six
patients. Disease activity was low (median CRP 1 mg/L, fecal
calprotectin 69 ug/g). Twelve patients (26.7%) had at least one
observation coded as suspected immunogenicity.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | 1 compartment, first-order absorption and elimination (ADVAN2 TRANS2) | Methods 2.3; Results 3.2.1 |
| `lka` | log(0.0113) 1/h, fixed | Table 3 (Ka, fixed); Table S1 |
| `lcl` | log(0.0170) L/h | Table 3 final model |
| `lvc` | log(9.14) L | Table 3 final model |
| `logitfdepot` | logit(0.750) | Table 3 F_SC; logit scale per Methods 2.3 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.00888 per kg from 73 kg, linear | Table 3 CLTBW; Eq. 1 |
| `e_ada_suspected_cl` | 0.700, proportional | Table 3 CLSUSP; Eq. 1 |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.257^2) = 0.06393 | Table 3 IIV_CL 25.7% |
| `etalvc`, `etalogitfdepot` | 0, held constant | Table 3 IIV_V, IIV_F_SC; Results 3.2.1 |
| `propSd` | 0.391 | Table 3 RUV 39.1%; proportional per Results 3.2.1 |
| CL equation | CL = 0.017 (1 + 0.70 SUSP)(1 + 0.00888 (TBW - 73)) | Eq. 1 |
| F applies to SC only | IV doses enter `central` with F = 1 | Methods 2.3 (F_SC); Figure 1 shows IV and SC observations in one fit |

# Covariate column naming

| Paper | Column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| TBW | `WT` | kg; linear, centred on 73 kg |
| SUSP | `ADA_SUSPECTED` | observation-level, time-varying 0/1; 1 = confirmed ADA, or an unexplained trough drop > 33% (Methods 2.2) |

# Replicating Figure S1: steady-state profiles by body weight

Figure S1 shows typical steady-state profiles after 120 mg SC every 2
weeks for 65, 73 and 81 kg (the 25th, 50th and 75th weight
percentiles). The model is solved for 12 doses (about 11 half-lives),
and the last dosing interval is plotted.

```{r figS1-sim}
tau <- 14 * 24
n_dose <- 12
t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, t_last, by = 24), seq(t_last, t_last + tau, by = 2))))

make_sc_events <- function(id, wt, susp = 0) {
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau, amt = 120, evid = 1,
    cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt, ADA_SUSPECTED = susp)
}

wt_groups <- c(65, 73, 81)
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(wt_groups), function(i) {
  make_sc_events(i, wt_groups[i])
}))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
# Typical-value solves use zeroRe(), for which rxode2's multi-subject
# "without 'omega'" warning is expected; only that warning is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = events, ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
sim_typ <- solve_typical(ev_typ, keep = "WT") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste0(WT, " kg"))

sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_last) |>
  ggplot(aes((time - t_last) / 24, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (days)", y = "Infliximab concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "Total body weight",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S1 of Vicente 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The model reproduces the digitised Figure S1 values (read by the
maintainers from the supplementary figure at the dose time and at the
peak of each curve):

```{r figS1-check}
fig_s1 <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("65 kg", "73 kg", "81 kg"),
  cmin = c(14.51, 13.32, 12.29),
  cmax = c(18.40, 17.19, 16.17)
)
typ_ss <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_last) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cmin = Cc[time == t_last], cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
chk_s1 <- dplyr::inner_join(typ_ss, fig_s1, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_fig"))
knitr::kable(chk_s1, digits = 2)
# Digitising precision of the figure is about 0.05 mg/L on a 12-18 mg/L
# axis; a wrong clearance, volume, bioavailability or weight slope moves
# these values by several percent.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(chk_s1$cmin_sim / chk_s1$cmin_fig - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(chk_s1$cmax_sim / chk_s1$cmax_fig - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

# Covariate effects on clearance

```{r cov-effects}
cl_typ <- function(wt, susp) 0.0170 * (1 + 0.700 * susp) * (1 + 0.00888 * (wt - 73))
cl_ratio_120_70 <- cl_typ(120, 0) / cl_typ(70, 0)
cl_ratio_susp <- cl_typ(73, 1) / cl_typ(73, 0)
cl_ratio_120_70
cl_ratio_susp
stopifnot(abs(cl_ratio_susp - 1.70) < 1e-12)
```

Under Eq. 1 a 120 kg patient has `r round(100 * (cl_ratio_120_70 - 1), 1)`%
higher clearance than a 70 kg patient; the Discussion quotes 46.1%, a
small difference that the printed equation does not reproduce (see
Assumptions and deviations). Observations coded as suspected
immunogenicity have 70% higher clearance, which at steady state lowers
the typical trough by more than half:

```{r susp-sim}
ev_susp <- dplyr::bind_rows(make_sc_events(1, 73, 0), make_sc_events(2, 73, 1))
sim_susp <- solve_typical(ev_susp, keep = "ADA_SUSPECTED") |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_susp |>
  dplyr::filter(time == t_last) |>
  dplyr::select(ADA_SUSPECTED, Cc) |>
  dplyr::rename("Suspected immunogenicity" = ADA_SUSPECTED, "Steady-state trough (mg/L)" = Cc) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# IV-to-SC switch

Switch patients carried IV records in the dataset; IV doses enter the
central compartment without the SC bioavailability. A typical 73 kg
patient on 5 mg/kg IV every 8 weeks who switches to 120 mg SC every 2
weeks:

```{r switch}
iv_tau <- 8 * 7 * 24
n_iv <- 6
switch_time <- n_iv * iv_tau
ev_switch <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = (seq_len(n_iv) - 1) * iv_tau, amt = 5 * 73, evid = 1, cmt = "central", rate = 5 * 73 / 2),
  data.frame(time = switch_time + (0:12) * tau, amt = 120, evid = 1, cmt = "depot", rate = 0),
  data.frame(time = seq(0, switch_time + 13 * tau, by = 24), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1, WT = 73, ADA_SUSPECTED = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
sim_switch <- solve_typical(ev_switch) |> as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_switch, aes(time / 24 / 7, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = switch_time / 24 / 7, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Infliximab concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = "Dashed line: first SC dose (2-hour IV infusions before it).") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort and observed troughs

The paper reports a median observed steady-state SC trough of 14.3 mg/L
(IQR 10.0-16.6) across the cohort, and mean troughs of 13.9 mg/L
(naive) and 14.8 mg/L (switch) in Table 2. A virtual cohort of 200
patients on the standard 120 mg every 2 weeks, with body weight drawn
log-normally around the Table 1 median (74 kg, IQR 65-82) and no
suspected immunogenicity, is simulated with IIV and residual error.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261162)
n_sub <- 200
wt_sd <- log(82 / 65) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
cohort_wt <- exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(74), wt_sd))
ev_coh <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) make_sc_events(i, cohort_wt[i]))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "120 mg SC q2w")
sim_coh <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_coh, keep = c("WT", "treatment")) |>
  as.data.frame()

troughs <- sim_coh |>
  dplyr::filter(time == t_last)
trough_summary <- data.frame(
  source = c("Observed (Vicente 2026 Results)", "Simulated with residual error"),
  median = c(14.3, median(troughs$sim)),
  q25 = c(10.0, unname(quantile(troughs$sim, 0.25))),
  q75 = c(16.6, unname(quantile(troughs$sim, 0.75)))
)
trough_summary |>
  dplyr::rename("Source" = source, "Median (mg/L)" = median, "Q1" = q25, "Q3" = q75) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Centre-only check: the observed troughs mix dosing intervals and
# include suspected-immunogenicity samples, so only the median is
# compared, with a tolerance wide enough for 200 subjects.
stopifnot(abs(median(troughs$sim) / 14.3 - 1) < 0.2)
```

```{r cohort-plot}
sim_coh |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_last) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes((time - t_last) / 24)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (days)", y = "Infliximab concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval at steady state, 120 mg SC every 2 weeks.") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the last dosing interval of the typical-value
solves, compared against the digitised Figure S1 values.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_dose <- ev_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_typ, id, treatment), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = t_last, end = t_last + tau,
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = fig_s1,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "cmin"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L")
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Weight" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA versus digitised Vicente 2026 Figure S1.")

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("tmax", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename("Weight" = treatment, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUCtau (mg*h/L)" = auclast, "Cavg (mg/L)" = cav) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The steady-state average concentration equals F x Dose / (CL x tau):
for 73 kg, 0.75 x 120 / (0.0170 x 336) = 15.8 mg/L. No row of the
comparison differs from Figure S1 by more than 20%.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV conversion.** Table 3 reports IIV_CL as 25.7% without stating
  whether it is a CV or the square root of the variance. It is
  converted as a CV, omega^2 = log(1 + 0.257^2) = 0.0639; reading it as
  sqrt(omega^2) would give 0.0660, a 3% difference in the variance.
* **IIV on V and F.** The paper held both at zero (Results 3.2.1);
  they are encoded as `fixed(0)` etas so that the model structure is
  explicit.
* **Weight centring.** Eq. 1 centres weight on 73 kg, described as the
  population median, while Table 1 reports a median of 74 kg. The
  equation value is used.
* **Clearance ratio in the Discussion.** The Discussion states that
  clearance rises by 46.1% from 70 to 120 kg; Eq. 1 gives 45.6%. The
  difference is within rounding of the slope and the equation is
  followed.
* **IV infusion duration.** The paper does not state the IV infusion
  duration; the switch illustration uses 2-hour infusions. Infusion
  duration has a negligible effect on troughs for this model.
* **Absorption rate.** Ka is fixed to the Hanzel 2021 estimate (0.27
  1/day = 0.0113 1/h); Table S1 shows the other parameters change by
  less than 10% when Ka is varied from 50% to 150% of this value.
* **Suspected immunogenicity.** `ADA_SUSPECTED` is defined from
  observed concentrations (a trough drop of more than 33%) as well as
  from ADA assays, so the 70% clearance increase is partly circular
  with the PK outcome; the authors describe the covariate as
  exploratory. For prospective simulation it is best treated as a
  scenario switch rather than a predicted quantity.
* **Virtual cohort.** Body weight is drawn log-normally from the Table 1
  median and IQR; all virtual patients receive the standard regimen and
  have no suspected immunogenicity.

Vicente B, Zazo H, Sanchez-Hernandez JG, Revilla N, Teixeira-da-Silva P.
Population Pharmacokinetics of Subcutaneous Infliximab: A Real-World
Study of Naive and Switch Patients. Pharmaceutics. 2026;18(9):1162.
doi:10.3390/pharmaceutics18091162
